title: Integral comparisons for a finite extension of coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E\subset S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sf-setting]. For a scheme $T$ in this setting put $R_T=\varprojlim_n(R/\ell^n)_T$ and $S_T=\varprojlim_n(S/\ell^n)_T$, the completed coefficient sheaves of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and set $C_T(-)=(-)_{\mathcal O_F}=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Integral bounded constructible categories mean [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Towers and normalized towers mean [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]; $R\varprojlim$ means the derived functor on strict towers, after restricting each level to the completed coefficient sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] and $f^!_{\mathcal O_E}=H_{f,\mathcal O_E}$ with its adjunction and purity map of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], and likewise for $F$.

1. $C_T$ sends $D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)$ to $D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_F)$, commutes with derived inverse limits of strict towers of $R_T$-module complexes, and has reductions
$$
 C_T(K)\otimes^L_{S_T}(S/\ell^n)_T\simeq
 (K\otimes^L_{R_T}(R/\ell^n)_T)\otimes^L_{(R/\ell^n)_T}(S/\ell^n)_T.
$$
2. For $M\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, the finite comparisons $b$ and $c$ of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image, det-sp-reduction-exceptional] for $R/\ell^n\to S/\ell^n$ are realized by maps in the derived categories of coefficient towers. Their derived limits give natural isomorphisms
$$
 C_Y(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M)\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_F}(C_XM),\qquad
 C_X(f^!_{\mathcal O_E}K)\simeq f^!_{\mathcal O_F}(C_YK).
$$
These comparisons carry the units and counits of the $E$-integral adjunction to those of the $F$-integral adjunction and intertwine the purity maps $\gamma_{f,\mathcal O_E}$ and $\gamma_{f,\mathcal O_F}$. For $E\subset F\subset L$ they compose to the comparisons for $E\subset L$, with derived tensor associativity identifications.
3. After inverting $\ell$ in the integral categories, using the rational categories and coefficient extensions of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], these are the comparisons
$$
 (Rf_{!,E}M_E)\otimes_E^L F\simeq Rf_{!,F}(M_E\otimes_E^L F),\qquad
 (f_E^*K_E(d)[2d])\otimes_E^L F\simeq f_F^*(K_E\otimes_E^L F)(d)[2d]
$$
for $M_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and $K_E\in D^b_c(Y,E)$, with the same unit, counit, purity and coefficient-composition compatibilities. Twists in the derived-complete and rationalized categories mean [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

proof.text: Write $A_n=R/\ell^n$, $B_n=S/\ell^n$, and $r=[F:E]$. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S_T$ is finite free of rank $r$ over $R_T$, and ordinary derived tensor on derived-complete objects agrees naturally with the strict-tower integral scalar extension. Applying [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] therefore proves constructible preservation in (1). Powers of $\ell$ can be used in these two nodes: if $\ell=u\varpi_E^h$, with $u$ a unit and $h\geq1$, then $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{hn})$, a cofinal family of the uniformizer powers; Over $F$ write $\ell=v\varpi_F^{h_F}$ with $v$ a unit and $h_F\geq1$; then $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_F^{h_Fn})$, again a cofinal family. The reductions of an integral constructible object are normalized with uniform Tor bounds by [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]. These are exactly the domains required for the finite comparisons, not merely arbitrary bounded finite-coefficient complexes. In the current reduction statement this is the ordinary derived category of modules over the completed sheaf $R_T$: the quotient maps are isomorphisms for every $1\leq m\leq n$, and any Tor interval $[a,b]$ of the integral input also bounds both Tor amplitude and cohomological support at every level. Thus no extra site comparison or level-dependent bound is being assumed.

source.place: paragraph (1), finite freeness, constructibility and the finite-Tor domains

proof.text: Choose an $R_T$-module basis of $S_T$ using the finite-free completed-sheaf theorem in step 1. The quotient identifications in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], applied to the complete discrete valuation rings $R$ and $S$ and the ideal $(\ell)$, identify $R_T/\ell^n$ with $(A_n)_T$ and $S_T/\ell^n$ with $(B_n)_T$. Reducing this single sheaf-module basis therefore gives compatible bases $(B_n)_T\cong(A_n)_T^{\oplus r}$. Forgetting the target coefficient action, $C_T$ is the functor $K\mapsto K^{\oplus r}$. Countable products of pro-etale module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and represent derived products by [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core]. Thus the canonical product/tensor comparison is the reindexing $\prod_n(K_n^{\oplus r})\cong(\prod_nK_n)^{\oplus r}$. It commutes with $1-s$, since its $n$-th component carries $x_n-t_nx_{n+1}$ to that same expression in each of the $r$ coordinates. For functoriality, use the total derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], not a choice of morphism between triangulated cones. Let $I_\bullet$ be a K-injective $R_T$-tower representative. Its finite sum $I_\bullet^{\oplus r}$ is K-injective: the Hom complex from an acyclic tower is a finite sum of acyclic Hom complexes. The ringed-topos identity morphism with structural map $R_T\to S_T$ has direct image restriction of scalars. Applying [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] to it identifies restriction of $R\lim$ of an $S_T$-tower with $R\lim$ of its restricted tower, compatibly with the projections. Restriction of scalars is exact and detects quasi-isomorphisms, so its derived functor reflects isomorphisms. The restricted coefficient-extended tower is $I_\bullet^{\oplus r}$, already K-injective over $R_T$ by the preceding Hom calculation; no K-injectivity over $S_T$ is needed for this computation. After this identification and the chosen basis, the canonical comparison $C_TR\lim I_\bullet\to R\lim C_TI_\bullet$ is the ordinary map $(\lim I_\bullet)^{\oplus r}\to\lim(I_\bullet^{\oplus r})$, an isomorphism. This proves the canonical derived comparison is invertible, including on morphisms; the product/$(1-s)$ calculation above describes the same comparison in its Roos triangle. It is $S_T$-linear since multiplication by any local section $s$ of $S_T$ acts by the same $R_T$-matrix on every level and on both products. Its definition by tensor and product projections is independent of the basis. For the reduction formula choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] compute its successive derived changes of rings. Both sides of (1) are represented by $P\otimes_{R_T}(B_n)_T$; the identification sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. These formulas commute with the quotient maps and with differentials, so they identify the whole reduction towers, including their morphisms.

source.place: paragraph (1), derived limits and the displayed reduction identity

proof.text: On coefficient towers let $C_\bullet$ be extension along $A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$. It is already exact on the abelian categories: the compatible basis above identifies its underlying complexes with a fixed finite sum, including transitions. The same finite-sum description preserves the common cohomological bounds. It preserves normalized constructible towers: for $m\leq n$ tensor balancing identifies $(D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}B_n)\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m$ with $(D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}B_m$, and [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] preserves the common Tor interval and constructibility. Form the compact-support coefficient map $b_\bullet:C_{Y,\bullet}Rf_{!,A,\bullet}\to Rf_{!,B,\bullet}C_{X,\bullet}$ by the proper-direct-image coefficient projection map followed by the open-extension tensor identification. The simultaneous section models in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] provide this specified composite as a morphism in the derived category of semilinear coefficient systems, not a choice of lifts of finite maps. The tower operations and their evaluations are those of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The evaluated composite is precisely the tensor comparison $b_n$ of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For $n\geq m$, the two paths $A_n\to B_n\to B_m$ and $A_n\to A_m\to B_m$ induce the same balanced tensor map: $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes\bar a b$. The coefficient-composition law of that node identifies the two composites of $b$. Thus these evaluations have the stated reduction compatibility. Each $b_n$ is an isomorphism, so $b_\bullet$ is an isomorphism by the detection assertion of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The current scalar-extension statement uses ordinary module sheaves over finite constant rings and the intrinsic finite-stratification constructibility condition. Our $A_n,B_n$ are precisely such constant coefficients, and $\ell$ is invertible on the standing schemes, as required for its Tate-line comparison.

source.place: paragraph (2), construction of the direct-image map of towers

proof.text: Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A,\bullet}$ and $G_A=f^!_{A,\bullet}$, and similarly for $B$. The adjunctions $P_A\dashv G_A$ with their specified counits $\epsilon_A$ are provided by [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Define $c_\bullet:C_{X,\bullet}G_A\to G_BC_{Y,\bullet}$ to be the $P_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $C_{Y,\bullet}\epsilon_A\circ b_{\bullet,G_A}^{-1}$. This is an actual tower morphism. Evaluation preserves these counits and adjunction transposes by [det-sp-tower-gluing, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], so its evaluation is the unique $c_{A_n,B_n}$ characterized in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. In particular it is an isomorphism at every level, hence an isomorphism of towers by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The quotient transitions of $G_A$ and $G_B$ are explicitly the quotient coefficient mates by [det-sp-tower-gluing](3). Applying [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](2) to the two paths from $A_n$ to $B_m$ identifies the two composites with $c_{A_n,B_m}$, proving the claimed reduction compatibility for $c$. The current compatibility statement applies here: all four quotient rings are finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, both mixed paths are unital maps, and the input at level $n$ has constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude by step 1. The separated finite-type scheme and smoothness hypotheses are precisely those fixed in the item.

source.place: paragraph (2), exceptional comparison as the tower counit transpose

proof.text:
The counit equation holds in the tower category by the definition just given:
$$\epsilon_B\circ P_Bc=C_Y\epsilon_A\circ b_{G_A}^{-1}.$$
For the unit equation transpose $G_B(b_M)c_{P_AM}C_X(\eta_{A,M})$ under $P_B\dashv G_B$. Naturality of $\epsilon_B$, the displayed counit equation, and naturality of $b$ turn its transpose into
$$b_M\, C_Y(\epsilon_{A,P_AM}\circ P_A\eta_{A,M})\,b_M^{-1}=1_{P_BC_XM}.$$
The last equality is the triangle identity in [det-sp-tower-gluing]; the transpose of $\eta_{B,C_XM}$ is the same identity. The adjunction bijection therefore proves the unit equation as a tower equality. For $R\subset S\subset U=\mathcal O_L$, the two direct-image comparison composites agree on the coherent models: both use the proper counit and the multiplication $(x\otimes s)\otimes u\mapsto x\otimes su$, then the open identification. The associativity coherences in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] give that equality before evaluation. Taking the counit transpose shows that the composite of the two exceptional comparisons is the exceptional comparison for $R\subset U$; this is exactly the mate-pasting formula [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1). Identity extensions give identities by its identity clause. This proves unit, counit and coefficient-composition compatibilities in the tower category itself.

source.place: paragraph (2), tower transposition arguments and composition of coefficient extensions

proof.text: Here is a justification of the purity identity that uses levelwise equality only between shifted degree-zero objects. Put $J_{A,T}=((A_n)_T)_n$ for $T=X,Y$, write $J_A=J_{A,Y}$, and put $\omega_A=G_AJ_A$; the source of the orientation below is $J_{A,X}(d)[2d]$. By [det-sp-tower-gamma](1) the tower orientation $a_{A,\bullet}:J_{A,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_A$ is an isomorphism in the derived tower category whose level $n$ is the finite diagonal orientation for $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_n$; with the evaluation identification of [det-sp-tower-gluing](3) this identifies $(\omega_A)_n$ with $(A_n)_X(d)[2d]$. Thus all evaluated cohomology groups outside degree $-2d$ vanish. Exact evaluation and levelwise kernels and cokernels in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] show that $\omega_A$ itself has cohomology only in degree $-2d$ in the coefficient-system category. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] it is its degree-$(-2d)$ sheaf placed in that degree. The finite orientations $\gamma_{f,A_n}(A_n):A_n(d)[2d]\to G_{A_n}A_n$ commute with quotient changes by [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3). Together with the transition description in [det-sp-tower-gluing](3), these give a morphism of the degree-$(-2d)$ coefficient sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] and shifting, it gives a uniquely specified isomorphism $o_A:J_{A,X}(d)[2d]\to\omega_A$ in the derived tower category. It equals $a_{A,\bullet}$: both are maps between shifted single-sheaf towers, and their levels agree, since by [det-sp-tower-gamma](2) at the unit (whose tensor map is the identity, step 7) the level $n$ of $a_{A,\bullet}$ is $\gamma_{f,A_n}(A_n)$. For $B$, [det-sp-tower-gamma](1) over $F$ identifies $(G_BJ_B)_n$ with $(B_n)_X(d)[2d]$, so exact conservative evaluation makes $G_BJ_B$ concentrated in degree $-2d$. Its degree-$(-2d)$ cohomology sheaf receives the compatible finite orientation maps from the twist sheaf: their quotient compatibility is [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3) and the target transitions are [det-sp-tower-gluing](3). Concentration and single-complex full faithfulness therefore yield the uniquely specified isomorphism $o_B:J_{B,X}(d)[2d]\to\omega_B=G_BJ_B$, equal to the orientation $a_{B,\bullet}$ of [det-sp-tower-gamma](1) over $F$ by the same comparison of levels. Twists commute with coefficient extension by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](3). The two maps $c_{J_A}C_X(o_A)$ and $o_B$ (with the twist source identification) have shifted degree-zero source and target, since $C_\bullet$ is exact. Their evaluations agree by [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3) at the unit object. Full faithfulness of the single-complex embedding reduces equality to equality of morphisms of coefficient sheaves; such morphisms are compatible families and their equality is componentwise. Hence $c_{J_A}C_X(o_A)=o_B$ as actual derived tower morphisms. No faithfulness claim for evaluation on general derived objects is made. In these two applications of finite purity compatibility the input is the coefficient unit, which is constructible and has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. The quotient maps and $A_n\to B_n$ need not be flat: the current statement permits every unital map of finite $\ell$-power-torsion rings. Its specified diagonal/DNC orientations are the finite orientations used here.

source.place: paragraph (2), orientation comparison of rank-one tower sheaves

proof.text:
The current projection statement [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a) has two finite-Tor inputs and requires specified etale-origin witnesses. These hypotheses hold here, rather than being automatic for arbitrary tower complexes. The normalized tower $K_\bullet$ has uniform cohomological and Tor bounds by definition. Step 6 identifies $\omega_A$ with the rank-one twist tower $J_{A,X}(d)[2d]$, so it is bounded, constructible levelwise, and each level has Tor amplitude $[-2d,-2d]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] choose bounded constructible etale-origin witnesses, retaining their comparison isomorphisms, for every $K_n$ and $(\omega_A)_n$. Their finite Tor intervals hold on the etale site by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii); the rings $A_n=A_{E,hn}$, with $h$ as in step 1, are within that statement's domain. For the $B$-inputs, step 3 gives bounded constructible levels of $C_YK$ with the original Tor interval, and $\omega_B\simeq J_{B,X}(d)[2d]$ has Tor interval $[-2d,-2d]$. Choose bounded constructible etale complexes realizing these two families of levels by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], now with $B_n=A_{F,h_Fn}$ from step 1, gives the specified intervals on these etale witnesses. If $w_n:\nu_X^*W_n\xrightarrow{\sim}(\omega_B)_n$ is the chosen witness isomorphism, a witness for $(C_X\omega_A)_n$ is the explicit composite $\nu_X^*W_n\xrightarrow{w_n}(\omega_B)_n\xrightarrow{(c_{J_A})_n^{-1}}(C_X\omega_A)_n$, using step 4 and $C_YJ_A=J_B$. This witness has Tor interval $[-2d,-2d]$ as well. Thus all projection inverses used below have both required finite-Tor witnesses. The current tower theorem requires witnesses levelwise, not a compatible tower of witnesses.

For an arbitrary normalized constructible $K_\bullet$, construct the tower tensor map $\tau_A:f_A^*K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_A\to G_AK_\bullet$ as the transpose of
$$P_A(f_A^*K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_A)\simeq K_\bullet\otimes^LP_A\omega_A\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{A,J_A}}K_\bullet.$$
The projection formula is a tower transformation by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2), and the adjunction is [det-sp-tower-gluing]. The specified finite tensor map is exactly this counit transpose by [def-pur-co-smoothness](2). At the coefficient unit it is the identity of $G_AJ_A$, since its transpose is $\epsilon_{A,J_A}$, with the tensor unit constraints. Thus the orientations $o_A$ constructed from the unit purity maps in step 6 are the finite diagonal orientations. Define $\gamma_{A,\bullet}=\tau_A\circ(1\otimes o_A)$ with twist reassociation. Its evaluations are the finite purity maps by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and the specified tensor-map definition just cited. In particular it is an isomorphism by levelwise detection. This is the tower purity map $\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet)$ of [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), whose derived limit is the integral purity map of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]: that node defines it as $t_{K_\bullet}\circ(1\otimes a_\bullet)$ with $t_{K_\bullet}$ the counit transpose of the same projection-formula composite as $\tau_A$, and $o_A=a_{A,\bullet}$ by step 6.

Here is the coefficient calculation before evaluation. Write $\pi_A(K,W):K\otimes^LP_AW\to P_A(f_A^*K\otimes^LW)$ for the tower projection map, including tensor symmetry, and similarly for $B$. Coefficient extension is monoidal and commutes with inverse image and shifts on the simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. With those source and target identifications, the projection maps satisfy
$$b_{f_A^*K\otimes^LW}\circ C_Y\pi_A(K,W)=\pi_B(C_YK,C_XW)\circ(1\otimes b_W).$$
For the proper piece this is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the tower ringed topoi: the horizontal morphisms are the identity topoi with the coefficient-ring maps, and the vertical morphisms are the proper direct image and its exact inverse image. No Cartesian-square or coefficient flatness hypothesis is needed there. The projection and exchange transformations are the counit-defined ones in [def-exchange-projection], with the simultaneous tower models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For the open piece its tensor identification commutes with coefficient extension: on the open the two maps send $(x\otimes y)\otimes s$ to $(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, and off the open both are zero. These formulas give the displayed equation for their compact-support composite. The equalities are in the tower category, not inferred from their evaluations.

Let $T_A=f_A^*K\otimes^L\omega_A$, identifying $C_XT_A$ with $f_B^*C_YK\otimes^LC_X\omega_A$. Under $P_B\dashv G_B$, the transpose of $c_KC_X\tau_A$ is, by the counit equation of step 5 and naturality of $b$,
$$C_Y\bigl((1\otimes\epsilon_{A,J_A})\circ\pi_A(K,\omega_A)^{-1}\bigr)\circ b_{T_A}^{-1}.$$
The transpose of $\tau_B(1\otimes c_{J_A})$ is, by naturality of the projection map and the same counit equation,
$$(1\otimes(C_Y\epsilon_{A,J_A}\circ b_{\omega_A}^{-1}))\circ\pi_B(C_YK,C_X\omega_A)^{-1}.$$
Inverting the displayed projection-compatibility square identifies these two composites. Adjunction therefore gives $c_KC_X\tau_A=\tau_B(1\otimes c_{J_A})$. Composing with $C_X(o_A)$ and using step 6 proves
$$c_KC_X(\gamma_{A,\bullet}(K))=\gamma_{B,\bullet}(C_YK)$$
with the pullback/twist source comparison. This proves purity compatibility for arbitrary complexes as an equality of tower morphisms.

source.place: paragraph (2), purity: projection-formula tensor map and the orientation comparison

proof.text: Apply these tower constructions to $\operatorname{red}_XM$ and $\operatorname{red}_YK$. The reduction identity of (1) identifies their $B$-extensions with the reduction towers of $C_XM$ and $C_YK$. By [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2), the derived limits of the direct-image towers are $Rf_{!,R}M$ and $Rf_{!,S}C_XM$. By [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], those of the exceptional towers are $H_{f,R}K$ and $H_{f,S}C_YK$. Using the canonical commutation with limits established in (1), $R\lim b_\bullet$ and $R\lim c_\bullet$ therefore have exactly the sources and targets in (2). They are isomorphisms because they are the image of tower isomorphisms under the functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The same integral-adjunction node says that the integral units, counits and purity maps are the derived limits of the tower ones. Applying this functor to the actual tower equations proved above gives the integral unit, counit and purity equations. The tensor associator commutes with this passage: on strict representatives its two composites send $((x\otimes s)\otimes u)$ to $x\otimes su$, and the limit comparison is defined by the same product projections. Thus the tower composition equation gives the integral coefficient-composition equation as well. The current direct-image statement takes the derived limit after restriction from $A_{n,Y}$ to the pulled-back completed sheaf $R_Y$ (and similarly for $S_Y$); these are exactly the restrictions fixed in the item. The compactification here is the coefficient-independent one fixed in the tower construction, so its stated comparison applies to both fields.

source.place: paragraph (2), derived limits and the integral adjunction/purity identifications

proof.text:
Use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]: its raw scalar localization has the same objects as the integral category, and its Hom groups are the integral Hom groups tensored with $E$. Thus every rational object has an integral representative. If $U$ is any integral $R$-linear functor, define its localized action on morphisms by $U_E(u\otimes a)=U(u)\otimes a$ and extend additively. Balancing follows from $R$-linearity; functoriality follows from $(v\otimes b)(u\otimes a)=vu\otimes ba$. The same formula localizes the components and naturality equations of integral natural transformations. An integral inverse localizes to an inverse. Applying this to integral coefficient extension gives precisely the rational extension defined in that node. Here $S[1/\ell]=F$: for $x\in F$, the valuation of $\ell^mx$ is nonnegative for sufficiently large $m$, so $\ell^mx\in S$. Tensor balancing gives $S\otimes_RE=F$, including for ramified extensions.

The rational compact-support functor on integral representatives is explicitly the localized integral compact-support functor in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; its integral limit is the functor identified in step 8. Its action on morphisms is the unique linear extension just described, since every localized morphism is a sum of pure tensors. Rational pullback and tensor are explicitly the localized integral operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Rational twists in these categories are the images of the integral twists by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; this is the rationalized convention fixed in the statement. Consequently localizing the two integral comparison isomorphisms of step 8 gives exactly the displayed functors of (3).

Finally the integral adjunction Hom bijections are $R$-linear: a transpose is the composite of the $R$-linear functor on a morphism with the fixed counit, and its inverse is composition with the fixed unit followed by the $R$-linear right adjoint. Both functors are $R$-linear on the tower models and remain so after the derived limit. Hence these are mutually inverse $R$-module maps, and we can tensor them with $E$. Their integral inverses, naturality equations and composition identities localize by the same pure-tensor formula, so the resulting bijections define the rational adjunction; its unit and counit are the images of the integral ones. The localized integral purity isomorphism identifies its right adjoint with $f_E^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Localizing the integral unit, counit, purity and coefficient-composition equations therefore proves every stated rational compatibility.
